sights.n: Kawasaki Daishi (川崎大師 平間寺)
sights.w: Head temple of the Chizan school of Shingon (founded 1128), one of the Kantō's busiest at New Year, reached down a lane of candy-makers chopping sweets to a drumbeat.

sights.n: Meguro Fudōson — Ryūsen-ji (目黒不動尊 瀧泉寺)
sights.w: Temple founded in 808 by Jikaku Daishi — the oldest Fudō sanctuary in the Kantō, with a dragon-mouth waterfall for ascetic bathing and a hillside of halls.
Shrine and grave of Yoshida Shōin, the Bakumatsu teacher executed in 1859, with a replica of his Shōka Sonjuku school — at the head of the old-school Shōinjinja-dōri arcade on the Setagaya tram line.
Large 1678 Jōdo temple in Okusawa whose three halls hold nine seated Amida Buddhas — ginkgo and maple colour in autumn, a short walk from Jiyūgaoka.
Adachi's big park on the Nippori-Toneri liner — cherry groves, a lake and the spring nemophila fields lit up for the Flower and Light Movement.
Where Edward S. Morse spotted a Jōmon shell midden from the train in 1877 and began Japan's first modern archaeological dig — now a small riverside park with the original strata on view.

sights.n: Tsukiji Outer Market (築地場外市場)
sights.w: The 400-odd stalls and counters that stayed when the wholesale market moved to Toyosu — tamagoyaki on sticks, oysters, knives, kaisen-don and dried bonito, best before noon.
The vermilion lacquered bridge over the Daiya River at the gateway to Nikkō's shrines — part of Futarasan Shrine and the UNESCO Shrines and Temples of Nikkō.
The 700 m promenade above Edo Castle's moat under some 230 cherry trees — Tokyo's most beloved hanami walk, with rowboats on the water below and night illuminations in season.

sights.address: Takaomachi, by Takaosanguchi Station, Hachiōji, Tokyo 193-0844
sights.w: Free nature museum at the foot of Mt Takao — a wall of mounted local wildlife and practical trail information before the climb.
